regime_context: The Hong Kong detector shows a narrow, two-legged leadership structure: Diversified Miners rank #1 but are NOT trend-gate eligible (gate blocks entry), while Banks (H + HK) rank #2 and ARE eligible with the strongest durability (0.68) and breadth (0.77). Only 4 of 17 themes pass the absolute-trend gate (Banks, High-Dividend Blue Chips, Conglomerates & Exchange, Tech Hardware & Semis) — a validation that helps cut drawdown here, but no theme has an ETF proxy, so nothing is scorable. Rotation is directional=false and one-narrative=false; momentum is a focus lens only.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Diversified Miners (non-eligible, rank #1) breach their own trend-gate to become eligible — that would mark a confirmed leadership handoff from the ranking into the tradeable universe. Condition to retire the watch: Miners' absolute-trend state flips to eligible or their rank falls below 5.

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: Banks are the only trend-gate-eligible theme that is also a top-2 momentum rank, with the highest durability (0.68) and breadth (0.77) on the board — the strongest staying-power combination available. The absolute-trend gate is the one validated risk-control leg here, and Banks pass it while the #1-ranked Miners do not, so a defensive lean toward the eligible leader is defensible on structural grounds, not return forecasting.
evidence: rank: 2 with score 1.185 behind only non-eligible Miners
theses.dissent: A bank-led tape in Hong Kong is often a late-cycle, rate-driven grind rather than a durable expansion; if H-share property collateral risk or a policy shift hits, bank breadth can unwind fast despite the gate. Also this theme is UNSCORABLE (no ETF proxy), so nothing here can actually be graded against a cheap tradable.
